summary:
# NOTES ON THREE BOOKS (for later lookup; not verbatim)

## BOOK 1: "Settling Day" (Nat Gould, Australian bush/turf novel, 30 chapters)

**Setting/people:** Wanabeen (Jim Dennis's station, NSW bush near Swamp Creek, nearest township; Potter's Shanty, Barragong police HQ ~10 mi away, Cudgegong station ~15 mi, Barker's Creek = Abe Dalton's gang camp). Jim Dennis: outcast, big powerful man, great horseman, hates the mother of his child; never smiles except with son. Willie (Willie Dennis), son, ~6 in ch.1, 12 at race time; little chap, jockey. Mare: Bess (Jim's). Dr Tom (Thomas Sheridan), drunk, kind ship's surgeon, Swamp Creek doctor, "Dr Tom"; dog Baalim (half dingo, ugly, "ass of a dog"); Dr Tom's black boy ~40. Sal, half-caste (black/white), found by Jim on his steps, raised by Jim; devoted to Willie; "King Charlie" = her tribe's chief; "the legend", curse. Maud Dennis = Jim's wife who deserted and claimed Willie wasn't hers; later returns dying (ch.25). Ned Glenn = coach driver (Sydney Lantern cartoon), killed by Seth Sharp/Dalton's men. Constable Fred Doonan = friend of Jim, later Sergeant, marries Sal. Sergeant Machinson = corrupt, shot dead at Barker's Creek by Dalton. Adye Dauntsey = police magistrate, Barragong. Rodney Shaw = Cudgegong owner, villain; manager Benjamin Nix; jockey Ben Madsley; horses Distant Shore, Seaweed (Seahorse's sons). Alec Beg = hand. Abe Dalton = gang leader, Barker's Creek; Seth Sharp = murderer. Aaron Hyam = bookmaker/Gum Tree Hotel, Swamp Creek; sons Moses. Price James = bookie. Silas Dixon = Wanabeen hand. Kit Cat, First Class, The Captain (Dalton's, jockey Jackson), Neptune (grey, by Seahorse out of La Perouse), Ashworth. Mrs. Maud, Potter (Samuel Potter, illiterate, forgery trial).

**Key events:**
- Ch1: Jim rides Bess to Swamp Creek; Willie (6) dying; Dr Tom drives buggy, saves him. Jim: "Settling Day."
- Ch2: Sal's backstory (mission, King Charlie, bolted). Jim: "Settling Day" re mother.
- Ch3: Potter's Shanty coach robbery; Jim suspected; Ned Glenn.
- Ch4: Maud deserted Jim for England/Sydney; claimed Willie not hers. Jim swears "settling day."
- Ch5: Strange stallion Seahorse (Rodney Shaw's) breaks into Wanabeen mob; Jim tames him with whip; Doonan helps.
- Ch6-8: Jim returns stallion to Cudgegong; Shaw seems changed (memory loss pretence, drinking). Dalton's men steal horse back; Jim retrieves it at Barker's Creek. Shaw plans to take Sal.
- Ch9-10: Dr Tom's poem story; Dr Tom visits Abe Dalton (dying), extracts oath to leave Jim alone.
- Ch11-12: Willie (12) chosen to ride Neptune in Swamp Creek Cup; Baalim.
- Ch13-14: Races set; Dalton's Captain; Dr Tom's bet; Sal warns Jim Shaw is enemy.
- Ch15: Willie struck on head by pestle, by Dalton.
- Ch16-18: Race: Neptune wins by short head over Distant Shore; Willie faints after.
- Ch19-21: Sal warns; Doonan; Ned Glenn shot dead by Seth Sharp; Dalton kidnaps Sal to Cudgegong for Shaw (£100); Dalton shoots black gin; Sal escapes via white-ant-eaten floor.
- Ch22-24: Assault on Barker's Creek; King Charlie's blacks; Machinson killed; Dalton, Sharp captured; Barker's Creek burned.
- Ch25: Maud arrives dying at Wanabeen; dies with Willie holding hand. Jim: "Settling day."
- Ch26: Jim confronts Shaw at Cudgegong; Shaw bleeds to death from back wound (Doonan's shot).
- Ch27-30: Trial at Bathurst; Chris Shaw (cousin) buys Cudgegong; Jim manages it; Sydney Cup with Grey Bird (by Neptune), Willie wins at 7st; Jim marries Molly Corbold; Sal marries Doonan; Jim buys Cudgegong. Ends with Jim's peace.

---

## BOOK 2: "Just a Girl" (Charles Garvice, 35 chapters — actually 30 numbered chapters)

**Setting:** Three Star Camp (Australian gold camp, Wally River, Ballarat); Dog's Ear camp (rival); Eldorado saloon (Dan MacGrath, bar); Mother Melinda (old woman nurse); Taffy (Welsh giant); Varley Howard (professional gambler, tall hat, languid, white hands, diamond scarf-pin, "Who plays this deal?"); Bill the postman; The Penman (old schoolmaster); Norman Druce (Lord Norman, Manor at Oakfield; mother Lady Druce; cousin Trafford; Lady Ada Lancing).

**Central figure: Esmeralda** (waif found in mail-sack by Bill; "won" by Varley at cards; named Esmeralda Howard; dark red-gold hair, dark brown eyes, freckles; shoots, rides, swims Wally River). Heiress to Gordon Chetwynde's two millions (mother dead; father's will). Lawyer Samson Pinchook (Pinchook, Pinchook & Becham, Grey's Inn). Lady Wyndover (guardian, Grosvenor Square, dyed hair, maid Barker; Madame Cerise dressmaker; Deepdale is her Surrey place).

**Events:**
- Ch1: Esmeralda found, won by Varley, named.
- Ch2: Childhood at camp; Penman's lessons; ridiculous delight; Varley says she'll marry him—he refuses.
- Ch3: Esmeralda saves Norman Druce from a shot at Dog's Ear; bullet in his leg; he's nursed at camp; delirium names her; proposal by river (she says "No").
- Ch5-6: Pinchook arrives; reveals inheritance; Varley insists she go; Three Star farewell; Lady Wyndover meets her.
- Ch7-8: London; Madame Cerise; Lady Blankyre's party; Lord Selvaine (Trafford's uncle); Esmeralda meets Trafford in Park, saves Lady Ada's horse.
- Ch9-11: Trafford introduced; Belfayre (Duke of Belfayre, failing; steward Helby; Lilias Selvaine, his cousin); Trafford's plan to marry money (Ada refuses him).
- Ch12-16: Trafford proposes in carriage at Shirley; Esmeralda accepts; Belfayre visit; duke's watering-place plan.
- Ch17-20: Engagement; wedding (Lady Ada bridesmaid); Ada overhears lovers; Esmeralda learns Trafford married for money.
- Ch21-23: Wedding night: Esmeralda: "No!" Separation at Deepdale.
- Ch24-27: Esmeralda leaves Deepdale for Belfayre? Norman's kiss in fernery seen by Trafford; Ada gives Esmeralda's... letter (Norman's old letter) to Trafford; accusation; Trafford divorce proposal; Esmeralda leaves at night, gives up ring; Duke dies in sleep (she kissed him).
- Ch28-33: Norman leaves to follow her; Trafford searches; Norman and Trafford reconcile at Raven Claim; Ada's deception explained.
- Ch34-36: Esmeralda returns to Three Star. Dog's Ear kidnaps her; Simon demands £200 ransom.
- Ch37-38: Ransom; escape from hut; reaches Wally-Wally.
- Ch39-41: Trafford duel with Varley at Raven Claim; Esmeralda throws herself between, shot in shoulder; survives.
- Ch42-44: Recovery; reconciliation; Trafford and Esmeralda reunited; Norman marries Lilias; Lady Ada gone abroad.

---

## BOOK 3: "The Runaways" (Nat Gould, 20 chapters, Hazelwell & Anselm Manor, Newmarket, Epsom)

**People:** Redmond Maynard, the Squire (Hazelwell), dog Bersak (wolf-hound); son Ulick Maynard (left after accusation about Janet Todd, two years earlier); Irene Carstone (ward, married Warren Courtly; Random = Ulick's bay hunter, painted by Irene); Warren Courtly (Anselm Manor, gambler, seduced Janet); Eli Todd (stud manager, ex-Hussars, daughter Janet Todd); Mrs. Marley (housekeeper); Bob Heather (groom, sweetheart Mary Marley, Irene's maid); Martha Dixon (Anselm housekeeper); Felix Hoffman (sharper, Feltham; mother Mrs. Hoffman); Fred May (trainer, Stanton House, Newmarket); Ben Sprig (jockey, "Ben"); Honeysuckle (old mare, colt foal born at midnight New Year's Eve); the Saint (grey, by Father Confessor out of Hilda, Ulick's, runs as "Mr. Lanark"); Dr Harding; James Bard (vet, Helton).

**Events:**
- Ch1: Snow; anniversary of Ulick's departure; Irene visits Squire; stays overnight.
- Ch2: Eli's account; Janet ran off same night as Ulick left; Squire accused Ulick.
- Ch3-4: Irene paints Random; letter from Felix Hoffman asking £5; she sends it.
- Ch5: Honeysuckle's colt foals New Year's midnight; Ulick secretly visits Eli.
- Ch6-7: Felix's story; Warren hid Janet at Feltham as "Mrs. Warren"; Holme Farm sold for £10,000.
- Ch8-9: Warren returns; Ulick buys the Saint (200 guineas from Fred May).
- Ch10-11: Saint wins Pastures Handicap at Kempton; Ulick sees Janet at Feltham; discovers Warren's guilt.
- Ch12-13: Squire and Ulick reconciled at Newmarket (Eli & Fred's plot); Squire sees the Saint.
- Ch14-15: Warren pressed by Felix; Irene visits Janet at Feltham; learns truth.
- Ch16: Coronation Cup at Epsom; the Saint beats Vulture by a short head.
- Ch17: Felix insults Warren in paddock; Warren confesses to Irene; threatens her.
- Ch18-19: Hunt at Helton; Warren challenges Ulick to leap Glen churchyard wall; grey falls; Warren dies, neck broken on Harewood's vault.
- Ch20: Irene and Ulick marry; Janet becomes Irene's maid; Squire's grandson born; happy ending.

---

*Note: Book 1 is a 30-chapter Nat Gould novel; Book 2 is Garvice's "Just a Girl"; Book 3 is Gould's "The Runaways". Keep separate.*
